Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Regional cloud availability zone nearby (same sub-region)
Comments: Regional zone nearby (South Africa AWS/Azure/Google) No local hyperscale
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source had been cited originally. Verified via official AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud region documentation plus an independent industry summary (Channelwise, Nov 2025): South Africa hosts AWS af-south-1 (Cape Town), Azure South Africa North/West (Johannesburg/Cape Town) and GCP africa-south1 (Johannesburg) — all in Botswana's sub-region — while no hyperscale provider has a zone or edge node inside Botswana itself. Botswana's own first national data centre (Digital Delta, Gaborone, opened Dec 2025) is a Tier III colocation facility, not a hyperscale cloud region, so it does not meet the bar for Code 4. This confirms Value Code 3 (regional availability zone nearby); code is unchanged/confirmed.
